context: Radial dendrogram with hierarchical edge bundling showing software module dependencies across 7 top-level modules and ~120 leaf nodes, with a tension slider controlling bundle tightness.
first_impression: A topological/relational visualization with no magnitude encoding, so most static honesty rules are inapplicable — what encoding exists is honest.
what_works: Color uses a Tol colorblind-safe ordinal palette mapped correctly to categorical module names; tension slider correctly computes beta = 1 - tension, and the cluster layout domain is fully data-driven via d3.cluster().size([2π, innerRadius]) with no hardcoded data values.
what_doesnt: Node dots have a fixed radius (3.5px) not tied to any data attribute, which is fine, but hover resizes them to 5px vs 2.5px asymmetrically rather than a consistent scale; edge color encodes source module only, silently ignoring target module identity, which could mislead directionality reads.
